title: apps/web SSO policy — gate with nz_access_token or leave public?
context: apps/web (AI chat, deployed on zantara.balizero.com / fly.dev) has NO middleware.ts, unlike the other 5 satellites (kita/mouth, drive, mail, calendar, knowledge) which all redirect to kita login when nz_access_token cookie is missing. apps/web GraphClient (src/lib/api/client.ts) accepts a Bearer token via setToken() but that method is never invoked in the current code — the app ships unauthenticated fetches to NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL. The backend hybrid_auth middleware DOES NOT list /api/query in public_endpoints, so real calls from apps/web to the graph-engine currently fail with 401 at the backend. Net effect: the UI loads without auth, but any actual query needs credentials that the app never provides. Users therefore hit a broken experience unless they are already logged into kita in another tab and some out-of-band token propagation happens.
question: Should apps/web be gated like the other satellites (redirect to kita login if nz_access_token is missing) OR should it stay publicly accessible (with the backend enforcing auth on /api/query as it already does) OR should the chat become explicitly public (add /api/query to public_endpoints and scope it down)?

options.label: Gate apps/web like other satellites (add middleware.ts with cookie check + kita redirect).
options.impact: Blocks anonymous use of the chat UI; matches security expectations for internal tooling.

options.label: Leave apps/web publicly accessible but document that the chat is only functional when logged in. Rely on the backend 401 as the gate. Add a friendly login CTA in the UI when a query fails.
options.impact: No middleware change; UX burden shifts to the UI layer.

options.label: Make the chat intentionally public — add a scoped anonymous tier to /api/query with rate limiting + audit logging, and keep UI ungated.
options.impact: Product change, not just security. Needs design review for rate limits and abuse prevention.

scope_note: Until a decision is made, air-a1 is NOT touching apps/web/. This escalation is logged from the security/auth-surface-hardening worktree so the rest of the audit fixes (CRIT-1 admin-dashboard, HIGH-6 portal RBAC, HIGH-7 admin emails) can land independently.
